title: Scaling decision stability safeguards & warm-cohorting postmortem
creator: Maya Kapoor
summary: During a production capacity event on 2026-01-22 we observed repeated premature scale-downs followed by insufficient scale-up during short bursts, which caused tail latency and increased request queuing for ~45 minutes across two customer clusters. This postmortem explains the root cause (a recent smoothing change to the scaling signal), the interim mitigations we executed, and the set of follow-up safeguards we implemented to prevent similar regressions.
timeline:
2026-01-22 09:12 UTC: First alerts from Grafana - rising queued requests and 95th latency > 2.5x baseline.
2026-01-22 09:15 UTC: KEDA controller initiated scale-down of several ReplicaSets after windowed metric fell below threshold.
2026-01-22 09:18 UTC: Sudden burst traffic began; scaled pods had cold starts and were insufficient to meet demand.
2026-01-22 09:35 UTC: On-call engaged, rolled back the recent smoothing change behind a feature flag; traffic stabilized after warm cohort rehydration.
2026-01-22 10:00 UTC: Incident declared resolved; started retrospective and root-cause analysis.
impact: Affected two customer-facing clusters in us-east-1 for ~45 minutes. 95th latency increased from 120ms to 850ms during the peak. Error rate (5xx) rose from <0.1% to 1.9%. Estimated customer-facing request failures ~0.4% of total requests during incident window. No data was lost; all requests retried successfully once scale recovered.
root_cause: A controller change (runtime PR #4821) replaced percentile-based smoothing with an exponential moving average (EMA) to reduce sensitivity. The EMA half-life parameter was tuned for smoothing at steady-state but did not account for short bursty traffic patterns, causing the scale-down decision to fire prematurely for pods in a cold cohort. Combined with a concurrent probe timing tweak (shorter liveness probe grace) this produced a false-negative scaling signal and increased cold-start exposure.
contributing_factors: Metric smoothing parameterization optimized for average traffic, not burst profiles
Feature flag rollout did not include a canary cohort with synthetic burst tests
Probe timing change reduced perceived pod readiness windows during scale-up
Lack of a multi-metric fusion policy (we relied primarily on CPU-percentile for this workload)
Runbooks lacked a clear playbook for 'scale-down oscillation with bursty workload' scenario
actions_taken: Rolled back the EMA-based smoothing change within 3 minutes of confirming correlation (feature flag toggle), restoring previous percentile smoothing
Temporarily increased warm-pool target size for affected clusters to 20% above baseline to buffer cold-starts
Reverted the liveness probe timing tweak to previous grace period to avoid premature evictions
Updated Grafana alerts to include multi-metric anomaly detection (CPU + request queue depth) to surface dangerous scale-down decisions earlier
action_items: ENG: implement a 'noise-gate' filter in the autoscaler to prevent small transient drops from triggering scale-downs (owner: Liam O'Connor, due: 2026-02-15)
ENG: add warm-cohorting support to maintain a minimum warmed pod set for bursty routes and make warm pools configurable per-route (owner: Priya Desai, due: 2026-03-01)
ENG: create a multi-metric fusion policy for scale decisions (CPU, request queue, p95 latency) and add unit+integration tests (owner: Rafael Gomez, due: 2026-02-22)
ENG/QA: add synthetic burst canary test that runs during feature flag rollouts to validate smoothing parameter changes (owner: QA Team, due: 2026-02-10)
DOCS: update autoscaling runbook with a specific playbook for oscillation during bursts and run a tabletop exercise with on-call (owner: Sarah Li, due: 2026-02-05)
SRE: instrument new dashboard panels for warm-cohort utilization and cold-start latency (owner: Tom Nguyen, due: 2026-02-12)
PM: schedule a post-release review gate for smoothing and probe changes (owner: Elena Ruiz, due: 2026-02-20)
follow_up: We will treat smoothing and probe changes as safety-sensitive for the next 3 releases: require burst canaries, enforce a minimum observation window for EMA parameter changes, and gate rollout to a single region before global rollout. A cross-team design doc (autoscaling-decision-safeguards) is being drafted to codify the noise-gating circuits, warm-cohort APIs, and multi-metric fusion approach.
notes: 01/25: Design doc draft posted to Confluence - request review from Runtime and SRE
01/28: Runtime team RFC accepted with suggested parameter ranges; agreed to feature-flagged rollout and canary tests
02/03: Initial implementation of noise-gate prototype merged behind flag - needs integration tests
